answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a locked stake with random audits. Every agent bonds collateral to receive one identity, and at random epochs the protocol posts a fresh challenge that only the real stateful agent can mirror. Failure or a recycled answer slashes the bond. To wander across thousands of fake personas, an attacker must post collateral for each one, so cost rises linearly with every Sybil, and an unlucky audit can wipe the whole pot. Even a sudden comet swarm of fresh accounts cannot dodge the bond, making mass impersonation economically pointless.
